t:
(a) 
The Subsistence Expense Act of 1926 and the Auto Mileage Act of February 14, 1931, are repealed. All Acts (other than appropriation items for examination of estimates in the field), applicable to civilian officers or employees of the departments and establishments, providing for reimbursement of actual travel or transportation expense, and all other Acts, general or special, which are inconsistent with or in conflict with the provisions of this Act (except such Acts or parts of Acts as fix or permit rates higher than the maximum rates established under this Act) are hereby modified, but only to the extent of inconsistency or conflict with the provisions of this Act: Provided, however, That Acts making appropriations for the fiscal years 1949 and 1950 (whether approved before or after the approval of this Act) which authorize or permit, in either general or specific terms, the payment of travel or transportation expenses without regard to the Subsistence Expense Act of 1926, as amended, or the Standardized Government Travel Regulations, shall be construed to authorize payment of such expenses from the appropriation concerned without regard to this Act.

 
    (b) 
Wherever provision is made in any law for the payment of per diem allowances to officers and employees in any branch or establishment of the Government not covered by this Act, in accordance with the rates provided in the Subsistence Expense Act of 1926, such law is hereby amended to provide for payment at the rates prescribed in or under this Act.

fable.w: This section only repeals and modifies earlier travel-expense statutes and conforms per diem rates for federal officers and employees. The tempting reading is that the mentions of the "Standardized Government Travel Regulations" and rates "prescribed in or under this Act" signal rulemaking, but these are references to existing or separately authorized rules, not a grant of rulemaking authority in this section. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: The Subsistence Expense Act of 1926 and the Auto Mileage Act of February 14, 1931, are repealed.

qwen_block.w: This section deals with the repeal and modification of laws regarding travel expense reimbursements for federal civilian officers and employees. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The actors involved are strictly internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: All Acts (other than appropriation items for examination of estimates in the field), applicable to civilian officers or employees of the departments and establishments, providing for reimbursement of actual travel or transportation expense... are hereby modified

opus.w: This section repeals earlier travel-expense statutes and makes other laws use this Act's per diem rates for federal officers and employees. Everyone involved is inside the federal government, and there is no comment period, hearing, outside consultation, advisory body, or right to sue. The reference to rates 'prescribed in or under this Act' and the mention of existing travel regulations point elsewhere; they do not give anyone new authority to make rules.
opus.s: such law is hereby amended to provide for payment at the rates prescribed in or under this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** You could read the mentions of the "Standardized Government Travel Regulations" and of rates "prescribed in or under this Act" as a grant of rulemaking authority, which would count as participation. That reading fails. The first phrase only refers to existing regulations in an appropriations exception. The second phrase only points to rates set elsewhere in the Act; this section itself gives no one the power to issue regulations. Otherwise, the section repeals and amends federal travel and per diem laws for federal employees, with no outside party involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section repeals previous acts and modifies laws regarding travel expense reimbursements for federal employees. It does not require consultation with, or participation from, any parties outside the federal government. The only entities mentioned are federal departments, employees, and Congress, which are all inside the government.
qwen_chat.s: The Subsistence Expense Act of 1926 and the Auto Mileage Act of February 14, 1931, are repealed. All Acts... applicable to civilian officers or employees of the departments and establishments... are hereby modified
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Act modifies how travel expenses are paid, it involves coordination with employees. However, the text only describes the repeal of old acts and the modification of laws regarding reimbursement rates for federal employees. There is no requirement for the government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or involve non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The actors involved are federal departments, employees, and Congress (via the Acts themselves), all of which are inside the federal government.
